prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_E:
Summary of key proposals

Economy and taxes
- Eliminate the deficit, move to a budget surplus from 2018–19, and run surpluses in normal times; no rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance.
- Raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the higher-rate threshold to £50,000; link the allowance to the Minimum Wage (“tax-free minimum wage”).
- £30bn further fiscal consolidation via departmental savings, welfare savings, and tackling tax avoidance/evasion; continued crackdown on aggressive tax planning.
- Support challenger banks, ring-fence retail banking, maintain the bank levy, and promote fintech and SME finance (e.g., Help to Grow).

Jobs, business and skills
- Create 2 million more jobs and 3 million apprenticeships; aim for highest employment rate in the G7.
- Youth Allowance for 18–21s with stronger work/training requirements; restrict automatic Housing Benefit for this group.
- Cut £10bn more red tape; review business rates; expand Start Up Loans; 1/3 of central procurement to SMEs; permanent Office of Tax Simplification.
- Publish gender pay gap data for large employers; aim to halve the disability employment gap; enforce the Minimum Wage and curb exploitative practices.

Infrastructure and digital
- Over £100bn infrastructure plan: £38bn for rail (electrification, HS2/HS3, Crossrail 2), real-terms freeze of regulated rail fares, smart ticketing and better compensation.
- £15bn for roads, major upgrades and pothole funding; promote cycling and ultra-low emission vehicles.
- Superfast broadband to 95% by end-2017; ambition for ultrafast; expand mobile coverage to 90% of landmass and lead on 5G.

Housing and local growth
- Double first-time buyers vs previous five years; extend Help to Buy schemes and introduce a Help to Buy ISA (25% bonus).
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount for under-40 first-time buyers); 275,000 additional affordable homes; 10,000 sub-market rental homes.
- Extend Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants with one-for-one replacements; prioritise brownfield, protect the Green Belt, support locally led garden towns.
- Devolve powers and budgets to city regions with elected mayors; allow councils to keep more business rates growth; keep council tax rises low via referendums.

Education and childcare
- Protect per-pupil funding; new literacy/numeracy standards; resits at secondary start if needed; EBacc subjects encouraged.
- Turn failing/coasting schools into academies; at least 500 new free schools; expand UTCs and degree apprenticeships.
- 30 hours’ free childcare for working parents of 3–4 year-olds; tax-free childcare up to £2,000 per child.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS spending each year; at least £8bn extra by 2020; implement the Five Year Forward View.
- Seven-day GP and hospital services by 2020; named GPs; same-day GP appointments for over-75s.
- Expand mental health access and waiting standards; sustain the Cancer Drugs Fund; faster access to innovative medicines; patient access to electronic records with opt-out.
- Integrate health and social care; cap residential care costs; increase dementia and carers’ support.

Welfare and poverty
- Overall welfare cap; two-year freeze of most working-age benefits from April 2016; reduce the household benefit cap to £23,000.
- Roll out Universal Credit; new measures addressing root causes of poverty; review benefit conditionality for treatable conditions with support to return to work.

Immigration
- Target net migration in the tens of thousands; reform EU welfare access (4-year contribution rule for tax credits/housing; end JSA for EU jobseekers).
- Stronger deportation and re-entry bans; extend “deport first, appeal later”; landlord checks; tackle illegal working; Controlling Migration Fund.
- English fluency requirement for public-facing roles; language progression for family visas.

Energy and environment
- Promote competition (smart meters by 2020); insulate 1 million more homes.
- Support shale gas with community benefits and a Northern Sovereign Wealth Fund; back new nuclear; end new subsidies for onshore wind and give locals final say.
- Meet climate commitments cost-effectively; expand offshore wind and low-carbon innovation.
- 25-year plan for nature; protect forests; 11 million more trees; stronger marine “Blue Belt”; more flood defences; tougher litter/fly-tipping penalties; animal welfare measures.

Crime, justice and security
- Continue police reform, transparency, technology use, and cyber capability; improve complaints system and diversity; targeted stop-and-search reforms.
- Ban new psychoactive substances; expand sobriety orders; modernise prisons and reduce contraband.
- Victims’ Law; stronger response to domestic abuse, FGM and child sexual exploitation.
- Replace the Human Rights Act with a British Bill of Rights; modernise courts; review legal aid.
- Update communications powers with oversight; new tools against non-violent extremism; tackle online radicalisation.

Pensions and older people
- Maintain the triple lock; introduce the single-tier pension; keep pensioner benefits.
- Cap care costs; no need to sell the home to fund residential care; greater freedom over pension savings and tax treatment.
- Raise the effective Inheritance Tax threshold for the family home to £1m for couples.

Constitution, EU and foreign policy
- English votes for English laws (including tax matters); implement new devolution for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; boundary reforms and “votes for life” for expats.
- In–out EU referendum by end-2017 after a renegotiation; protect Single Market interests; seek repatriation of powers and end “ever closer union.”
- Maintain strong Armed Forces (minimum army 82,000), renew the nuclear deterrent, invest in equipment and reserves; uphold NATO commitments.
- Keep aid at 0.7% of GNI with outcomes on health, education, WASH, vaccines, girls’ rights and crisis response.

TEXT_C:
Summary of key proposals (ideological framing removed)

Public finances and economy
- Allow modest annual increases in public spending while reducing deficit and debt as a share of income; balance current spending over the medium term.
- Prioritise infrastructure investment, productivity, and job creation; create a sovereign wealth/energy fund when conditions allow.
- Raise revenues via restoring the 50p top income tax rate, a bankers’ bonus tax, higher bank levy, a mansion tax, abolishing non-dom status, tackling avoidance, reviewing pension tax relief, and reversing the married couples’ allowance.
- Seed-fund a national business development bank; expand export finance; strengthen late-payment protections; raise the Employment Allowance to £6,000 by 2019–20; provide stability for Annual Investment Allowance.
- Cut and devolve Air Passenger Duty, consider a VAT cut for hospitality, and expand support for creative industries (including fairer BBC spend, games sector incentives).
- Reintroduce a post‑study work visa; City Deals for all cities; increase northern UK infrastructure focus; connect Scotland to HS2; expand broadband/4G with a telecoms Universal Service Obligation.
- Support a UK target of 100,000 affordable homes annually and further housebuilding in Scotland.

Work, pay and equality
- Increase the minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; promote the living wage; equal pay audits for large firms; strengthen maternity discrimination laws; remove VAT on sanitary products.
- Modernise union balloting (including secure online voting); restore 90‑day consultation for large redundancies; increase employee representation on boards; address exploitative zero‑hour contracts.

Welfare and pensions
- Abolish the Bedroom Tax; halt and review Universal Credit and PIP rollout; reverse DLA to PIP change; raise the work allowance by 20%; uprate benefits at least by cost of living.
- Increase Carer’s Allowance to match Jobseeker’s Allowance; review sanctions/conditionality; protect Savings Credit; oppose restricting housing benefit for 18–21s; disregard war disablement pensions in means tests.
- Support a single‑tier pension at £160/week with the triple lock; review state pension age rise to 67; retain winter fuel allowance; tackle pension charges.

Health, education and childcare
- Increase UK health spending (yielding about £2bn extra for Scotland by 2020–21); protect the NHS from privatisation; expand mental health funding; integrate health and social care; fund delayed discharges and new medicines.
- Expand free childcare to 30 hours/week for 3–4 year‑olds and eligible 2‑year‑olds; maintain free university tuition; deliver 30,000 Modern Apprenticeships; expand Educational Maintenance Allowance.

Energy, climate, and environment
- Fund ECO from general taxation; require suppliers to pass through wholesale price cuts; ensure prepayment parity; earlier winter fuel payments for off‑grid pensioners.
- Support a fracking moratorium; oppose renewal of the UK nuclear deterrent.
- Match ambitious carbon‑reduction targets; prioritise offshore wind, sustain onshore wind, support hydro, CCS, storage, island interconnectors, and transmission charging reform; expand community energy and renewable heat.

Rural, postal, and food policy
- Protect Royal Mail’s Universal Service Obligation, retain a 30% public stake, and pursue return to public ownership over time.
- Secure fair CAP convergence funding; simplify CAP; implement discard ban practicably; return seabed leasing net income to coastal communities; devolve food levies; promote food and drink, including whisky duty reform.

Justice, policing, data
- Retain 1,000 additional police officers; keep court fines revenue in Scotland; seek VAT exemption for police and fire services.
- Oppose blanket data retention; support targeted, overseen measures against extremism.
- Devolve regulation of fixed‑odds betting terminals and payday lending.

Governance and rights
- Strengthen MP recall; adopt Single Transferable Vote; replace the House of Lords with an elected chamber; extend voting to 16–17‑year‑olds; refine lobbying rules while easing limits on charity campaigning.
- Maintain the Human Rights Act and ECHR commitments; advance gender balance on public boards; support a Race Committee; review immigration detention; appoint an LGBTI rights envoy.

EU, trade, foreign and defence
- Support continued EU membership with a “double‑majority” requirement for any UK exit; expand devolved roles in EU decision‑making; exempt public services from TTIP; retain European Arrest Warrant.
- Maintain 0.7% GNI for international development; exclude defence spend from aid; audit developing‑country debt; require parliamentary approval for military action; support a two‑state solution in the Middle East.
- Refocus defence on northern/Arctic needs; procure maritime patrol aircraft and patrol vessels in Scotland; increase regional transparency in defence spend; build Type 26 frigates and refit carriers in Scotland; improve support for service personnel and families.

Devolution
- Implement the Smith Commission swiftly and fully, without effective vetoes.
- Seek further devolution toward full financial responsibility; prioritise employment policy (including minimum wage), welfare, business taxes, National Insurance, equality, and broadcasting during transition; keep Barnett Formula until full responsibility is achieved.

Judge whether TEXT_E or TEXT_C aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_E" | "TEXT_C"
}
